instruction: I'm watching a lecture video in VLC while taking notes. When I click on other windows to type, the video player goes behind them and I can't see it. Could you enable the 'always on top' setting so the VLC window stays visible above my other applications?

parameters.window_name: lecture.pdf — 6.006 Introduction to Algorithms, Lecture 2: Data Structures

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.click({SCREEN_WIDTH_HALF}, {SCREEN_HEIGHT_HALF}); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.explanation: Task requires user to enable VLC's always on top setting (video-on-top=1). The evaluator uses custom check_video_on_top__e48d3a20 metric to verify that video-on-top setting is set to 1 in VLC config file.
metadata.verification: Verified with custom function check_video_on_top__e48d3a20. Expected value: video-on-top=1 (enabled). Default is 0 (disabled).

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly reads VLC config file (vlcrc) which stores the always-on-top setting
Metric logic correctly parses the config file for 'video-on-top=' line and compares to expected value
Expected value 'video-on-top=1' is semantically correct for enabling always-on-top feature
Complete coverage: instruction has single requirement (enable always on top) and evaluator checks exactly that
Postconfig appropriately kills and reopens VLC to ensure settings are flushed to config file
Proper error handling for FileNotFoundError and general exceptions with 0.0 fallback
Data flow is correct: getter extracts right state, metric compares right aspect, expected value is accurate
